# Safety by limits, not by approval: testing an AI system that has no approval queue

> Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system.

## Abstract

Ultrastable R&D (Ultrastable): A common belief holds that the way to keep an AI system safe is to have a person approve each step. Ultrastable has no approval queue. It bounds its essential variables, verifies every deploy live, reverts what fails, and pauses only for acts that are both irreversible and bound to the owner's identity. We test the alternative to approval on every step: declared limits on what matters, checks that can fail, live verification, automatic revert and one narrow stop for acts that are both irreversible and identity-bound. Each property is measured; the ones that fall short are open work. 4 of 6 are met today; each one that is not is an open work item with a closing probe, and this paper is regenerated from the measurements after every merge.

## The study

Is human approval of every step what keeps AI safe?. Ultrastable R&D, Ultrastable; own R&D question set, regenerated from this system's records, version 2026-11-21. Data: This system's own ledgers: closed pull requests read from GitHub, the deploy record, the criticality ticks, the ultrastability ledger and the loop registry.

## Findings, mechanisms and measurements

### S1. Everything that matters has limits (safety)

**The study:** Belief: without a person watching, nothing stops a system drifting. Test: share of declared essential variables that have limits. (Essential variables)

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- ASHBY-1 (`foundation/ultrastability.py`): an essential variable with no limits fails the check

**Measured here:** share of declared essential variables that have limits (doctrine/ultrastability.json): 1.0 (n = 13). Target >= 1.0. Verdict: **met**.
Source: doctrine/ultrastability.json.

### S2. Unreviewed changes are not reverted more (quality)

**The study:** Belief: changes merged without human review get undone. Test: reverts on main per merged pull request. (Git history)

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- AUTO-SHIP-CLEAN-1 (`seed/worker/src/sweeper.js`): only a change whose checks pass merges
- RUNWAY-1 (`foundation/redmain.py`): a red main is repaired by bisection and the smallest revert

**Measured here:** commits on main whose subject starts with Revert, per merged pull request in the window: 0.0 (n = 64). Target <= 0.05. Verdict: **met**.
Source: git log of main, subjects starting with Revert.

### S3. What ships is proven live (reliability)

**The study:** Belief: an unapproved deploy could be anything. Test: share of uploaded deploys proven live against their commit. (Deploy record)

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- HANDOFF-1 (`deploy/deploy-workers.mjs`): a deploy counts only after the live read-back matches its commit

**Measured here:** share of uploaded deploys proven live against their commit: 1.0 (n = 40). Target >= 0.95. Verdict: **met**.
Source: ops/deploys.jsonl (same window).

### S4. The system corrects itself when a limit is crossed (safety)

**The study:** Belief: only a person can correct a system that goes out of bounds. Test: share of second-order steps that brought a variable back inside its limits and were kept. (Ultrastability ledger)

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- ASHBY-SEARCH-1 (`foundation/ultrastability.py`): the second loop keeps changing a parameter until the variable holds, and reverts a step that did not help

**Measured here:** share of second-order steps that brought the variable back inside its limits and were kept: 0.0 (n = 77). Target >= 0.25. Verdict: **not-met**. Open item: `Q-RES-safety-by-limits-2026-S4`.
Source: ops/ultrastability.jsonl verdicts.

### S5. Little work is thrown away (quality)

**The study:** Belief: without approval, a system produces work that has to be discarded. Test: share of closed pull requests closed without merging. (Pull request record)

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- FAILURE-RESOLVE-1 (`foundation/failure_audit.py`): a failing detector files its own item with root-cause suspects, so failed work becomes a fix

**Measured here:** share of closed pull requests closed without merging: 0.36 (n = 100). Target <= 0.2. Verdict: **not-met**. Open item: `Q-RES-safety-by-limits-2026-S5`.
Source: GitHub REST pulls?state=closed, last 100 closed pull requests, fetched 2026-11-21T09:30:00Z.

### S6. One halt stops everything (safety)

**The study:** Belief: an autonomous system cannot be stopped. Test: every registered loop has a server-side owner and closing probe, so one switch reaches each of them. (Halt and loop registry)

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- HALT-1 (`seed/worker/src/budget.js`): one worker variable or committed file stops every cron, webhook and workflow job

**Measured here:** share of registered loops that declare a closing probe and a server-side owner: 1.0 (n = 112). Target >= 1.0. Verdict: **met**.
Source: instances/ultrastable/loop-registry.json (declared).

## Limits

- Scale. One organization: 100 closed pull requests (64 merged) over 0.75 days. Our numbers describe this system; they are not a causal estimate and are not compared with the study's effect sizes as if they were.
- Who wrote the changes. 80% of merged pull requests in the window were opened by code agent sessions run under the owner's account, not by the system's own loops. The latest criticality tick puts the system in the subcritical regime with 0 self-originated deploys, so most of the work measured here was started from outside.
- Review by construction. Ultrastable has no human review step, so a short open-to-merge time is partly a consequence of the design. The real test of the design is quality: the revert and deploy-verification findings, which can fail.
- Revert share counts commits whose subject starts with Revert; a fix that undoes a change without that word is not counted, so the figure is a lower bound.
- Source. Own r&d question set, regenerated from this system's records, version 2026-11-21; its findings may change in later versions.
